You are the database administrator for an e-commerce platform that processes customer orders and manages payment transactions. When users transfer funds between their accounts, the system ensures that funds are only deducted after the user confirms the transaction. Simultaneously, the platform allows customers to place orders, reflecting inventory changes in real-time to prevent overselling of items. To safeguard against system failures, the application creates backup copies of database pages for quick recovery. This layered database recovery approach aims to maintain data integrity and reliability while providing a seamless user experience, even in the event of a transaction error or system crash.

I. Identify and describe the approach taken for handling fund transfers and explain why this method is suitable for this scenario.

ii. Explain the backup strategy implemented for recovering the database. How does this method enhance the recovery process, and what are its limitations?

Design an Enhanced Entity-Relationship (EER) diagram for the following university academic management system. Your diagram should clearly specify entities, attributes (including keys), relationships, participation constraints, cardinalities, and any specialization or aggregation used. State any assumptions you make. The university manages its academic programs, courses, faculty, students, and course offerings.
• The university is organized into several Faculties (e.g., Engineering, Science, Arts). Each faculty has a FacultyID, name, and dean.
• Each faculty is divided into multiple Schools (e.g., School of Computer Science, School of Physics). Each school has a SchoolID, name, and head.
• Each School offers several Programs (e.g., B.Tech CSE, M.Sc Physics). Each program has a ProgramID, name, duration, and degree type.
• Each Program consists of multiple Courses. Each course has a CourseID, title, credits, and semester offered.
• Lecturers teach courses. Each lecturer has a LecturerID, name, email, and specialization. A lecturer can teach multiple courses, and a course can be taught by multiple lecturers (possibly in different semesters).
• Students enroll in one program but can register for multiple courses each semester. Each student has a StudentID, name, email, year of study, and program enrolled.
• For each Course Offering (a course taught in a specific semester), record the CourseID, Semester, Year, LecturerID(s), and number of students enrolled.
• Students receive grades for each course offering. Grades are recorded as A/B/C/D/F.
• Some courses are electives and can be chosen by students from any program, while others are core and mandatory for specific programs.
• There are specializations for students: Undergraduate and Postgraduate. Postgraduate students may have a thesis title and a supervisor (who is a lecturer).
• The university tracks prerequisite relationships between courses (e.g., Course A is a prerequisite for Course B).
